events.titleEn: Boat images appear in Scandinavian art
events.summaryEn: Schematised boats appear in Scandinavian art; the earliest known example is incised on a bronze sword from Rørby, Denmark. Boats are among the most frequent motifs on the engraved rock faces of Sweden.
events.selectionNote: Dates the start of a motif that runs through Scandinavian Bronze Age art.

date.noteEn: The Met gives an approximate century.

events.titleEn: Scandinavia and the Baltic take up bronze
events.summaryEn: Peoples of Scandinavia and the Baltic region begin to acquire bronze technology. With no local tin or copper, they expand long-distance trade with central and southern Europe, and amber becomes their most valuable export.
events.selectionNote: Records the arrival of bronze technology in Scandinavia and the amber trade that paid for it.

date.noteEn: The Met dates Shang control of this area to about 1600 BCE and gives no founding year.

events.titleEn: The Shang dynasty rules a large area of northern China
events.summaryEn: The Shang dynasty controls a large area of northeastern and north-central China. Zhengzhou, thought to be a cult centre, is among its major sites, and Anyang serves as capital from about 1300 BCE. Shang workshops cast ritual bronze vessels for wine and food in multiple ceramic moulds.
events.selectionNote: The catalog records Erlitou, the Yin capital (1300 BCE) and the Zhou conquest (1050 BCE), with no record for the start of Shang rule.

date.noteEn: The Met dates the New Kingdom to about 1550–1070 BCE and places Ahmose's reunification at its start without a separate year.

events.titleEn: Ahmose I reunites Egypt and founds Dynasty 18
events.summaryEn: The Theban king Ahmose I reunites Egypt and founds Dynasty 18, the first dynasty of the New Kingdom. His successors, Thutmose III in particular, extend Egyptian influence through the Levant to the borders of the Hittite empire.
events.geographyEn: Thebes and the Nile valley, Egypt
events.selectionNote: The catalog records Hyksos rule from Avaris (1650–1530 BCE). This record covers the Theban reunification that opens the New Kingdom.

date.noteEn: The Met places the loss at the beginning of the New Kingdom and Egyptian control to the fourth cataract by about 1450 BCE.

events.titleEn: Kerma loses Lower Nubia to Egypt
events.summaryEn: Kerma loses control of Lower Nubia when the Egyptian kings of Dynasty 18 begin campaigns against Upper Nubia. By about 1450 BCE Egypt rules Nubia as far south as the fourth cataract through a viceroy, the King's Son of Kush.
events.geographyEn: Lower and Upper Nubia, present-day Egypt and Sudan
events.selectionNote: The catalog records the founding of Kerma (2500 BCE) and its monumental burials. This record covers the loss of Lower Nubia.
